section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the call "Vayikra" to Moshe precedes speech, originating from the Essence of Ein Sof, and is drawn into the speech of Torah, with the small aleph indicating Moshe's self-nullification enabling this revelation, especially in the context of offerings.
section.t: And this is, "And He called to Moshe, and G-d spoke, saying: 'When a man brings an offering...'"
For this, that to all the utterances etc. a call preceded—an expression of endearment—is also a precedence in level,
for the call is above speech.
And it goes so far that it says "Vayikra" (And He called) without specifying who is the caller,
because the call is from the Essence of Ein Sof, which is above Havayah.
Nevertheless,
from the fact that the call was specifically before speech
(even though a call—an expression of endearment—is a matter in its own right,
and not a preparation for speech),
it is understood
that the call also relates to the speech.
And it can be said
that the speeches, sayings, and commandments of Torah are from Havayah,
as it is written regarding all the speeches etc. of Torah
(and also in the speech of this verse)
"and G-d spoke,"
and the call is from the Essence, as above.
And the concept of "Vayikra" and "Vayedaber" (He called and He spoke) is the drawing down and revelation of the Essence
(which is above Torah)
into the speech of Torah.
And in general, it is the drawing down of Torah as it is rooted in the Essence.
And one can connect this with what is written, "Vayikra" with a small aleph,
and according to the teaching of the Alter Rebbe
(who said to the Tzemach Tzedek when he was three years old)
that the small aleph of "Vayikra" indicates the humility and self-nullification of Moshe,
for although he knew his own levels,
nevertheless he did not consider himself important,
and on the contrary, this knowledge brought him to be even more lowly in his own eyes
(as explained there at length).
And it can be said that one of the reasons that the small aleph, which alludes to the self-nullification of Moshe, is in the word "Vayikra,"
is
that through his self-nullification he became a vessel for the revelation of "Vayikra,"
the drawing down and revelation of Torah as it is rooted in the Essence
(similar to what was explained above regarding the matter of Yissachar).
And based on this, it will be understood why "Vayikra" is said in the portion of offerings,
even though a call preceded all the utterances etc.,
because this matter of Torah being rooted in the Essence is revealed primarily in that Torah deals with the laws of offerings,
to refine the world and make it a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that every Jew has an aspect of Moshe and his self-nullification, so the call "Vayikra" applies to each one, empowering them in the spiritual service of offerings as preparation for the literal offerings in the Third Temple.
section.t: And it is known
that in every single Jew there is an aspect of Moshe,
including the self-nullification of Moshe.
And from this it is understood
that the matter of "Vayikra el Moshe" (And He called to Moshe) applies also to every single Jew.
And especially when one studies this verse.
And through this, empowerment is also drawn to him for the service of offerings in a spiritual sense,
and this becomes a close preparation for the service of offerings in its literal sense,
and there it will be done before You according to the commandment of Your will,
in the Third Temple, which will be built speedily in our days,
and very soon.
